text: dsh-session-flags 是一个面向 DSH Web 客户端的会话管理插件。它在会话行、悬停操作和菜单中提供颜色旗标入口，并增加可搜索的“已标记会话”侧栏页面。用户可从八种颜色中为会话添加或清除标记，重命名颜色，并按会话标题、工作区或颜色名筛选结果；面板按颜色分组并可直接返回对应会话。标记与颜色名称保存在 DSH home 下的本地 JSON 文件中，状态由 Host 提供给 Client。使用需要 DSH 版本 >=0.2.0-rc.2，不需要额外 API key。

dsh-session-flags adds color flags to DSH sessions and a searchable sidebar. Assign or clear one of eight colors, rename colors, and filter by session title, workspace, or color. Results group by color and open the chosen session. Data stays in a local JSON file; no API key is needed.
想给重要的 DSH 会话加上不同颜色的标记，方便之后认出来。

I want to label DSH sessions with colors and quickly find them again in a searchable panel.
dsh-session-flags 的功能「会话颜色旗标」：从会话行悬停操作或“…”菜单打开选择器，为会话设置八种颜色之一，也可清除旗标；选择结果保存到 Host 管理的状态文件。
dsh-session-flags 的功能「已标记会话搜索」：打开侧栏面板后，可按会话标题、工作区名称或颜色名筛选已标记会话，结果按颜色分组并可直接跳回会话。

dsh-session-flags README · dsh-session-flags：A flag is not a pin: pins reorder the list, flags label it. Use one color for “waiting on me”, another for “refactor in progress”, a third for “read tomorrow” — and rename the colors to match your own workflow.

dsh-session-flags README · Highlights：- **A flag on every flagged session row.** A small flag glyph sits in the session-row leading seat, right before the title, while the row is idle; the row's own status dot takes precedence when a session needs attention.
- **One click on hover.** The row's hover strip carries a flag button; its hollow state tells unflagged rows apart at a glance.
- **A “Set flag” row in the session “…” menu.** It sits between “Fork” and “Archive” and previews the current color.
- **Named colors.** Each of the eight palette colors can be renamed. Names show up in the hover card, the picker, and the menu, so the color system can carry your own vocabulary.
- **A searchable “Flagged sessions” panel.** A sidebar panel row opens a page that groups every flagged session by color, shows each color's name, and jumps straight back to the conversation. Search matches session titles, workspaces, and color names.
- **Bilingual UI** (English / Simplified Chinese) following the GUI language.
- **Durable, local, private.** Flags live in one JSON document under the DSH home, owned by the plugin's Host half. No network calls, no telemetry, no changes to the sessions themselves.

dsh-session-flags README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness Desktop (or the Web GUI) **0.2.1-rc.2**. The package declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.0-rc.2"`, and named installs are checked against that range before the package manager runs.
- The plugin is a normal independent DSH plugin package (Host half + Client browser bundle); it installs into a profile, not into the application.

dsh-session-flags README · From npm：Published as the unscoped npm package [`dsh-session-flags`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-session-flags):

```bash

dsh-session-flags README · plugin is enabled without a second step.：dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-session-flags
```

In the GUI this is **Plugins → Add plugin**, typing `dsh-session-flags`. Either way, reload the profile afterwards — restart the Harness so the new Client bundle is registered. On the official DSH Desktop app prefer the app's own **Settings → Plugins** page: that profile belongs to the app's plugin manager, and the CLI cannot change it while the app is running.

dsh-session-flags README · Marketplaces：Third-party listings are independent of npm. The community **dsh-market** reads the curated [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) registry; a listing is one pull request that adds `data/plugins/<owner>__<repo>.yml`, and the market app picks the entry up from that registry (usually within a day of the PR merging). The exact submission file and release checklist are in [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md).

dsh-session-flags README · Marketplaces：The official Harness ships **no plugin market**. Its optional *custom plugin markets* bundle (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle`) adds a **Discover** tab where the user adds market index sources; the community catalog is published as a format-1 index at `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dsh-plugin-catalog/index.json`. Turn it on from **Plugins → More → Experimental plugins → Custom plugin markets**, add that source, and search for `dsh-session-flags`. With the bundle on, the agent can browse the same indexes through the read-only `plugin_market` tool.

dsh-session-flags README · Usage：| Where | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Session row, leading seat | Shows the flag color while the row is idle (status dots win while a session needs attention). |
| Session row, hover strip | Flag button → opens the **Set session flag** dialog. |
| Session “…” menu → **Set flag** | Same dialog, reachable without hovering. |
| Session hover card | Colored dot plus the color's current name. |
| Dialog → **Manage flag colors** | Rename each of the 8 colors; blank a name to fall back to the localized default. |
| Sidebar → **Flagged sessions** | Searchable page with every flagged session, grouped by color name. Search matches the session title, its workspace, or the color name. |
| Panel row hover → **×** | Clear that session's flag without opening the conversation. |
| Panel header → **Manage colors** | Same color-name manager, right where the list is. |
dsh-session-flags README · Usage：Choosing “No flag” clears the flag. Names and flags are saved as soon as you confirm; the dialog reports a failure instead of closing when the Host rejects a write.

dsh-session-flags README · How it works：```
src/
  shared/         palette + wire protocol shared by both halves
  host/           Cordis plugin: owns flags.json, registers exact Fetch routes
  client/         Cordis plugin: locale copy, styles, slot contributions, dialogs

dsh-session-flags README · How it works：**Host half** (`name` / `inject` / `apply`). It needs only `ctx.connection` and registers three exact Fetch routes below `/api/dsh-session-flags` (`state`, `set-flag`, `color-names`) with `ctx.connection.fetch.register`. Each response uses the Connection convention `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, error: { code, message } }`. The document is persisted atomically (write temp file + rename) with serialized mutations, so concurrent UI actions cannot lose a write.
dsh-session-flags README · How it works：**Client half.** It registers a locale namespace, one `<style data-plugin-css>` element, and six slot contributions:

dsh-session-flags README · How it works：| Slot | Entry |
| --- | --- |
| `sidebar.session.row.leading` | `FlagMark` — colored glyph in the leading seat |
| `sidebar.session.row.hover` | `FlagHoverTag` — dot + name in the hover card |
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.row.action` | `FlagRowAction` — flag button in the hover strip |
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` | `FlagMenuItem` — “Set flag” menu row |
| `shell.overlay` | `FlagDialog` — picker + color-name manager |
| `sidebar.panellist` | `FlagPanelIcon` — sidebar row for the flagged-session panel |

dsh-session-flags README · How it works：All six are registered through `ctx.slots.inject`, so they appear when the owning slot declares itself and are disposed with the plugin. State flows through two observable sources (`FlagsStore`, `DialogStore`) handed to the framework as `hooks`, which yields typed `useFlags(selector)` / `useDialog(selector)` hooks in every seat — no cross-slot imports.

dsh-session-flags README · How it works：**The panel** is a seventh contribution: a keyed entry in the layout's `main` slot under the panel id `dsh-session-flags`. The sidebar row and the page share that id (a panellist list id addresses the matching main panel). The page reads the Session and Workspace Controller snapshots through the framework's standard selector hooks, projects them plus the flag document with `buildFlagPanel` (pure, unit-tested), and navigates by delegating to the Workspace UI service (`uiWorkspace.openSession`). That service is injected through `ctx.inject`, so profiles without the workspace UI still keep every row-level flag feature.

dsh-session-flags README · How it works：**Why the Host owns storage.** The Desktop host boots `dsh` with `--port 0`, so the GUI gets a different loopback origin on every launch; a browser `localStorage` document would be per-launch. A JSON file under the DSH home is stable across launches, windows, and Web/TUI clients.

dsh-session-flags README · How it works：**Styles** are plain CSS injected as `<style data-plugin="dsh-session-flags" data-plugin-css="dsh-session-flags/flag.css">`, with all chrome reading `--dsw-*` theme tokens (the same mechanism official client packages use) instead of adding a CSS runtime dependency. Flag colors are the one exception: they are user data and are painted from the persisted hex.

dsh-session-flags README · Develop：```bash
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck     # tsc --noEmit (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess)
pnpm test          # vitest: palette, Host store, Client store, dialog store, panel projection, SSR seats
pnpm build         # tsdown: lib/index.js (ESM, Host) + lib/client.js (CJS ModuleLoader)

dsh-session-flags README · Develop：The Client bundle is a CommonJS ModuleLoader factory (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`) with `react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, and `@deepseek-ai/*` left external for the running Harness to resolve — the same shape official client packages and other third-party plugins use. `dsh.client.inject` lists the client services/packages the bundle expects loaded first.

dsh-session-flags README · Develop：Compatibility target: official packages are pinned at `0.2.1-rc.2` as dev dependencies for types; the only runtime peer is `@deepseek-ai/cordis ~4.0.5` (optional, supplied by the host loader). `engines.dsh` declares the supported host range (`>=0.2.0-rc.2`), which is also what named installs are preflight-checked against. The plugin degrades quietly (no marks, no dialog) when a slot or service is missing rather than patching the host or the application.

dsh-session-flags README · Data location：`$DSH_HOME/session-flags/flags.json` (`$DSH_HOME` defaults to `~/.dsh`). The Host resolves the directory through the Harness `dshHomePath` service. Document shape:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "flags": { "<session-id>": "red" },
  "colorNames": { "red": "重点项目" }

Unknown fields and invalid ids are dropped on load, so a partially corrupted file never blocks the feature.
